screen: Production Story proof review (desktop 1440), stage 4 pass 1

expected_differences: The Lab shows Content overview, not a Story-proof workflow. Production correctly replaces its gallery, caption editor and scheduling sections with proof, requirements, creator information and a payment decision.
Demo Coffee Co., Tyler Okafor, the coffee creative, submission date, credit balance and notification counts are production records rather than the Lab’s fictional content.
Submitted, Creator not verified, Instagram not connected and no recorded follower count are legitimate states. None should be replaced with verified or eligible fixture states.
Approve and pay $25.00 correctly expresses immediate payment. The creator receives $21.25 after the 15% fee; the fee is not added to the business’s $25.00 payment.
keep: The mineral canvas, graphite navigation and proof housing, white decision surface, restrained borders and shadow-free application regions.
The recognizable mark, typography, 200px navigation rail and 32px desktop content gutter.
The intact portrait creative, literal Submitted status, recorded Story URL, 24-hour requirement and explicit eligibility gaps.
The statement that TapMart has not checked Instagram and that approval is the check.
The amount-bearing approval button, Request changes, Reject, View person and Campaign navigation.
review.readiness_note: The core workflow, real states and payment semantics remain visibly exposed; this capture does not establish that their handlers work. Do not sign off the 1440px screen until the composition, evidence inspection, posted-time presentation and money hierarchy are corrected.

drift.change: Retain the two-column review, but make the left source assembly visibly occupy its 472px column: keep the 315px proof housing and place the supplied creative beside it at 141px wide with a 16px internal gap. Use a 24px gap to the decision plane. Start that plane 24px below the source top, and place creator, Story facts, eligibility, note and payment controls together on that white plane with 24px padding, 0px structural radius and no shadow. Keep requirements beneath the source assembly.
drift.why: The proof housing ends around x547 while the facts begin at x728, leaving approximately 181px of unexplained canvas. The supplied creative is below the proof, and the white surface contains only the final payment block. This fragments the source-to-commitment relationship instead of transferring it.
drift.where: Main proof assembly and right-hand decision region

drift.change: Add a visible Submitted proof label at 14/20px and ink Open proof and Open supplied creative controls with minimum 44px targets. Open each corresponding original record in the existing inspection experience. Preserve source ratio with object-fit: contain, use 4px corners for ordinary proof media and 0px corners for the supplied Story sheet.
drift.why: Only the supplied thumbnail is explicitly identified. The large image looks like the same creative, and neither source has a visible original-inspection control. At the current thumbnail size, the reviewer cannot reliably compare fine details before authorizing payment. Matching imagery alone is not evidence of incorrect data binding.
drift.where: Large proof preview and supplied-creative thumbnail

drift.change: Render the recorded posted timestamp with date, time and timezone at 14/20px, for example using the format MMM d, yyyy · h:mm a z. If only a date exists, retain it and append Time not recorded. Keep Posted at 9am attributed to Their note; do not promote that note into a verified timestamp or infer a completed live period.
drift.why: Posted currently shows only Sep 12, 2026, although the decision depends on a 24-hour live requirement. The creator’s separate 9am claim does not resolve the missing recorded time or timezone.
drift.where: Posted row beside Must stay live

drift.change: Give the business debit a dedicated payment anchor: Pays now at 14/20px followed by $25.00 in Archivo 700 at 44/48px, tracking -0.025em, with tabular lining numerals and ink color. Put Creator receives $21.25 after the 15% fee and Credit now: $17,887.00 on separate 14/20px supporting lines. Preserve Approve and pay $25.00 and the existing payment calculation.
drift.why: The payment is currently a bold fragment inside a two-line body paragraph. The button carries more financial emphasis than the amount itself, weakening the approved money-first hierarchy and making debit, net payout and available credit harder to distinguish.

review.why: The shared shell and material treatment are convincingly transferred, and the screen preserves honest eligibility and immediate-payment semantics. The main failure is compositional: a small isolated proof, a supplied sheet underneath, detached facts and a separate payment strip do not form the approved source-to-decision assembly. Missing visible evidence inspection, date-only posting information and body-sized payment emphasis also weaken this consequential review.
review.verdict: The production workflow visibly survives, but Frame Shift is only partially transferred and this desktop screen is not ready for release.
